Stat. § 47a-4 (Terms prohibited in rental agreement), retrieved verbatim from cga.ct.gov on 2026-06-05 (reflects P.A. 23-207, which added the (a)(9) late-charge cap and redesignated the heat/utility surcharge as (a)(10)). § 47a-4(b): 'A provision prohibited by subsection (a) of this section included in a rental agreement is unenforceable.' Citations deep-link to the section anchor on the official CGA chapter page. ALL rules remain status=draft-unverified: regex, severity, and plain-English framing must be reviewed by a CT tenant attorney / legal-aid clinic before public conclusions.

rules.title: Waiver of the tenant's legal rights or remedies
rules.description: Per § 47a-4(a)(1), a lease cannot make the tenant waive or forfeit rights or remedies under the landlord-tenant statutes (or any statute/ordinance) unless that law expressly permits waiver. Such a provision is unenforceable.
rules.tenant_explainer: A lease can't quietly strip away rights the law gives you. Broad language making you 'waive any and all rights' generally can't be enforced.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(1) & (b)
citations.quote: A rental agreement shall not provide that the tenant: (1) Agrees to waive or forfeit rights or remedies under this chapter and sections 47a-21, 47a-23 to 47a-23b … or under any section of the general statutes or any municipal ordinance unless such section or ordinance expressly states that such rights may be waived … (b) A provision prohibited by subsection (a) of this section included in a rental agreement is unenforceable.

rules.title: Confession of judgment
rules.description: Per § 47a-4(a)(2), a lease cannot authorize the landlord to confess judgment on a claim arising out of the rental agreement. Unenforceable.
rules.tenant_explainer: You can't sign away your right to defend yourself in court. A clause letting the landlord 'confess judgment' against you isn't enforceable.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(2) & (b)
citations.quote: A rental agreement shall not provide that the tenant: … (2) authorizes the landlord to confess judgment on a claim arising out of the rental agreement … (b) A provision prohibited by subsection (a) of this section … is unenforceable.

rules.title: Landlord exculpation / tenant indemnifies landlord
rules.description: Per § 47a-4(a)(3), a lease cannot make the tenant agree to exculpate or limit the landlord's liability arising under law, or to indemnify the landlord for that liability or related costs. Unenforceable.
rules.tenant_explainer: Your landlord can't use the lease to escape responsibility for their own negligence, or make you cover their legal costs. 'Hold harmless' / 'not liable for anything' clauses generally don't hold up.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(3) & (b)
citations.quote: A rental agreement shall not provide that the tenant: … (3) agrees to the exculpation or limitation of any liability of the landlord arising under law or to indemnify the landlord for that liability or the costs connected therewith … (b) A provision prohibited by subsection (a) of this section … is unenforceable.

rules.title: Waiver of interest on the security deposit
rules.description: Per § 47a-4(a)(4), a lease cannot make the tenant waive the right to interest on the security deposit owed under § 47a-21. Unenforceable.
rules.tenant_explainer: Your security deposit earns interest that's owed to you. A clause making you give up that interest can't be enforced.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(4) & (b)
citations.quote: A rental agreement shall not provide that the tenant: … (4) agrees to waive his right to the interest on the security deposit pursuant to section 47a-21 … (b) A provision prohibited by subsection (a) of this section … is unenforceable.

rules.title: Self-help eviction (dispossess without a court order)
rules.description: Per § 47a-4(a)(5), a lease cannot let the landlord dispossess the tenant without resort to a court order. Unenforceable; Connecticut requires a court eviction (summary process).
rules.tenant_explainer: A landlord can't legally lock you out or force you out on their own — they have to go to court. Any clause saying otherwise isn't enforceable.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(5) & (b)
citations.quote: A rental agreement shall not provide that the tenant: … (5) agrees to permit the landlord to dispossess him without resort to court order … (b) A provision prohibited by subsection (a) of this section … is unenforceable.

rules.title: Distraint / landlord's lien on the tenant's property for rent
rules.description: Per § 47a-4(a)(6), a lease cannot make the tenant consent to the distraint of their property for rent. Unenforceable.
rules.tenant_explainer: Your landlord can't seize or hold your belongings to cover unpaid rent. A clause letting them do that isn't enforceable.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(6) & (b)
citations.quote: A rental agreement shall not provide that the tenant: … (6) consents to the distraint of his property for rent … (b) A provision prohibited by subsection (a) of this section … is unenforceable.

rules.title: Landlord's attorney's fees over the statutory cap
rules.description: Per § 47a-4(a)(7), a lease cannot make the tenant pay the landlord's attorney's fees in excess of fifteen per cent of any money-damages judgment against the tenant. Flag attorney's-fee clauses so the cap can be checked.
rules.tenant_explainer: If you lose a rent case, the most you can be made to pay toward the landlord's lawyer is 15% of the judgment. Watch for clauses demanding 'all' or 'reasonable' attorney's fees with no cap.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(7) & (b)
citations.quote: A rental agreement shall not provide that the tenant: … (7) agrees to pay the landlord's attorney's fees in excess of fifteen per cent of any judgment against the tenant in any action in which money damages are awarded … (b) A provision prohibited by subsection (a) of this section … is unenforceable.

rules.title: Late charge before the grace period, or over the statutory cap
rules.description: Per § 47a-4(a)(8)-(9), a lease cannot charge a late fee before the § 47a-15a grace period expires, demand 'reduced rent' only if paid before the grace period, or charge a late fee exceeding the § 47a-15a cap. § 47a-15a(b) caps a late charge at the lesser of $5/day (max $50) or 5% of the delinquent payment, and allows only one late charge. Flag late-fee clauses to check timing and amount.
rules.tenant_explainer: Connecticut gives you a grace period before rent is 'late' (9 days for a month-to-month tenancy). A late fee charged before that isn't allowed, and once it does apply it can't exceed $5/day up to $50, or 5% of the late rent — only one charge.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(8)-(9) & (b)
citations.quote: A rental agreement shall not provide that the tenant: … (8) agrees to pay a late charge prior to the expiration of the grace period set forth in section 47a-15a or to pay rent in a reduced amount if such rent is paid prior to the expiration of such grace period; (9) agrees to pay a late charge on rent payments made subsequent to such grace period in an amount exceeding the amounts set forth in section 47a-15a.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-15a — grace period & late-charge cap
citations.quote: If rent is unpaid when due and the tenant fails to pay rent within nine days thereafter or, in the case of a one-week tenancy, within four days thereafter … 'grace period' means the nine-day or four-day time periods … Such late charge may not exceed the lesser of (1) five dollars per day, up to a maximum of fifty dollars, or (2) five per cent of the delinquent rent payment … The landlord may not assess more than one late charge upon a delinquent rent payment.

rules.title: Heat or utilities surcharge when included in rent
rules.description: Per § 47a-4(a)(10), if heat or utilities are included in the rental agreement, a lease cannot make the tenant pay a heat or utilities surcharge. Context-dependent on whether utilities are included.
rules.tenant_explainer: If your rent includes heat or utilities, the landlord can't tack on an extra 'surcharge' for them.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(10) & (b)
citations.quote: A rental agreement shall not provide that the tenant: … (10) agrees to pay a heat or utilities surcharge if heat or utilities is included in the rental agreement … (b) A provision prohibited by subsection (a) of this section … is unenforceable.
